section_summary: This section consists chiefly of 1947 applications and diplomatic correspondence concerning permission for foreign merchants, commercial representatives, travelers, and returning residents to enter or transit occupied Japan. It documents quota administration by the Inter-Allied Trade Board, referrals to SCAP and War Department permit officials, security checks, and restrictions caused by food and housing shortages. Additional material concerns baggage limits, missionaries’ food shipments, Japanese repatriates’ freight, and procedures for air passengers transiting Japan.

subfiles.title: Greek Embassy request for Form DS-513 sets
subfiles.from: A. S. Liatis, Royal Greek Embassy
subfiles.to: Albert E. Clattenburg Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests three sets of applications for permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Liatis asks the State Department to supply three sets of Form DS-513.

subfiles.title: Reply supplying Form DS-513 sets
subfiles.to: A. S. Liatis, Royal Greek Embassy
subfiles.about: Responds to the Greek Embassy’s request for entry forms.
subfiles.summary: The Department encloses three requested sets of Japanese-entry application forms.

subfiles.title: Translation of Mexican note concerning Roberto Gómez Cisneros
subfiles.about: Acknowledges a U.S. request for information about Gómez Cisneros’s proposed mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Mexico will provide the requested information once it is received from Mexican authorities.

subfiles.title: Mexican note concerning Roberto Gómez Cisneros
subfiles.about: Spanish original acknowledging the request for information about Gómez Cisneros.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy says Mexican authorities are obtaining information on Gómez Cisneros’s proposed Japanese mission.

subfiles.title: Budapest telegram denying clearance for Doroteo Kavayo
subfiles.about: Reports denial of Allied Control Council clearance to Dr. Kavayo and his children.
subfiles.summary: ACC clearance was denied to Dr. Doroteo Kavayo and his children.

subfiles.title: Hellmold letter concerning Denise Bickart’s exit permit
subfiles.about: Offers additional information to expedite Denise Bickart’s return to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hellmold thanks Hutcherson and offers assistance with military review of Bickart’s return.

subfiles.title: Denise Anne Bickart alien departure application
subfiles.about: Applies to leave the United States and rejoin her husband near Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Bickart identifies herself as a French Kobe resident seeking permanent return to her husband, René Bickart, after wartime internment and recuperation abroad.

subfiles.title: Denise Bickart affidavit supporting return to Japan
subfiles.about: Explains her Japanese residence, wartime internment, health-related departure, and wish to rejoin her husband.
subfiles.summary: Bickart requests permission to return to Kobe after recuperating in Europe from her wartime internment.

subfiles.title: Norwegian request for businessman quota
subfiles.about: Seeks places for four Norwegian businessmen among the 400 authorized foreign commercial visitors.
subfiles.summary: Norway asks U.S. assistance in obtaining four Japanese-entry places for Norwegian businessmen.

subfiles.title: State Department reply on Norway’s business quota
subfiles.about: Explains Norway’s provisional allocation of two businessmen per twenty-one-day period.
subfiles.summary: The Department explains that heavy demand forced reduced national quotas. Norway receives two business travelers every twenty-one days, subject to renewals approved by Norway and SCAP, and applications must follow Circular No. 8.

subfiles.title: Panamanian transmittal of Missri application
subfiles.about: Transmits two copies of Teófilo Homsany Missri’s Japanese-entry application.
subfiles.summary: Panama forwards Missri’s application and requests prompt notice of the decision.

subfiles.title: Teófilo Homsany Missri application to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Requests entry to Kobe for approximately three months to purchase dry goods.
subfiles.summary: Panamanian merchant Missri seeks to travel via San Francisco to Kobe to buy textiles and ready-made goods for sale in Panama.

subfiles.title: Translation of Panamanian Missri transmittal
subfiles.about: English translation of Panama’s letter transmitting Missri’s application.
subfiles.summary: Vallarino forwards two application copies and asks to be informed of the outcome.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Teófilo Missri
subfiles.about: Records departmental checks concerning Missri and his firm.
subfiles.summary: Checks found only a benign reference and a favorable wartime trade report on Homsany Hermanos.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Missri application to the War Department
subfiles.about: Forwards Missri’s application under the quota for “other” nations.
subfiles.summary: Hunt asks the Military Permit Section to submit Missri’s case to SCAP under the residual business quota.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Missri application
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the application and explains quota-based military review.
subfiles.summary: The Department is forwarding Missri’s application to military authorities and will notify Panama when a decision arrives.

subfiles.title: Iranian request for Hussein Touty’s entry
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Hussein Touty to visit Japan for import-export business.
subfiles.summary: Iran seeks Japanese entry for Shanghai merchant Hussein Touty to arrange bilateral trade.

subfiles.title: Conversation concerning Touty’s incomplete application
subfiles.about: Explains to Mr. Aram that Touty must submit Form DS-513 with missing personal and travel data.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg advises the Iranian Embassy to provide a completed application before military referral.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Hussein Touty
subfiles.about: Records searches for information about Hussein Touty.
subfiles.summary: Departmental checks found no information concerning Hussein Touty.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Touty application to the War Department
subfiles.about: Forwards Touty’s application under the quota for “other” nations.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard asks military officials to submit Touty’s business-entry application to SCAP.

subfiles.title: U.S. Commercial Company transmittal concerning Chosaku Oishi
subfiles.about: Forwards correspondence concerning Oishi’s requested shipping permit.
subfiles.summary: Parks sends Hibbard Black’s inquiry and the company’s reply regarding Oishi’s shipment.

subfiles.title: U.S. Commercial Company reply to George Black
subfiles.about: Directs Black to the State Department for Oishi’s shipping-permit request.
subfiles.summary: The company disclaims responsibility and refers Oishi’s case to Richard Hibbard.

subfiles.title: George Black request for Oishi shipping permit
subfiles.about: Requests authority to ship Oishi’s merchandise to Japan before his repatriation.
subfiles.summary: Black seeks a permit for roughly 85 cubic feet and 2,500 pounds of Oishi’s merchandise.

subfiles.title: Instruction to deny Cabada’s transit through Japan
subfiles.about: Directs that Peru be told Cabada must omit Japan from his itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Japan’s food and housing shortages preclude Cabada’s proposed civilian transit.

subfiles.title: Referral requesting advice on Cabada memorandum
subfiles.about: Requests advice on the attached Peruvian memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Espy asks JA or FC to recommend action on Cabada’s transit request.

subfiles.title: Peruvian Embassy memorandum on Eduardo Cabada
subfiles.about: Requests an eight-day Japanese transit stop for Eduardo Cabada.
subfiles.summary: Cabada, traveling on Peruvian sugar and jute business, seeks to transit Japan between China and Hawaii without conducting business there.

subfiles.title: State Department denial of Cabada transit
subfiles.about: Denies Cabada permission to transit Japan under prevailing entry restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Because SCAP limits civilian entry to officials, military or religious travelers, and essential businessmen, Cabada’s transit request cannot be granted. A later application may receive favorable consideration if conditions improve.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Isidoro Azrak
subfiles.about: Records initial security and commercial checks on Isidoro Azrak.
subfiles.summary: Initial checks found no derogatory information, with a later annotation noting additional review.

subfiles.title: Translation of Panamanian Azrak transmittal
subfiles.about: English translation forwarding two copies of Azrak’s application.
subfiles.summary: Panama submits Azrak’s application and requests prompt notice of the decision.

subfiles.title: Panamanian Azrak transmittal
subfiles.about: Spanish original transmitting Isidoro Azrak’s application.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy forwards two application copies and asks to be notified of the result.

subfiles.title: Isidoro Azrak application to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Requests a year in Japan to investigate and resume his prewar trading business.
subfiles.summary: Azrak seeks entry to Yokohama and Kobe to recover business records, merchandise, bank funds, and property, and to revive exports to customers abroad.

subfiles.title: State acknowledgment of Azrak application
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Azrak’s application and explains its quota-based military review.
subfiles.summary: The Department is forwarding Azrak’s application and will report the military decision.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Azrak application to the War Department
subfiles.about: Forwards Azrak’s application under the quota for “other” nations.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard requests SCAP consideration of Azrak as a Panamanian businessman.

subfiles.title: Mexican request for Enrique Bravo’s entry
subfiles.about: Requests a permit for Enrique Bravo to serve as Mexico’s commercial representative in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Mexico appoints Bravo to liaise with SCAP on restoring Mexican-Japanese commerce.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Enrique Bravo
subfiles.about: Records checks concerning Bravo and a possibly related newspaper accusation.
subfiles.summary: No definitive derogatory information was found; an accusation against Enrique González Bravo could not be linked conclusively.

subfiles.title: Conversation about Bravo’s missing application form
subfiles.about: Requests a completed entry form for Enrique Bravo from the Mexican Embassy.
subfiles.summary: Madrid agrees to obtain a completed application after Wolberg supplies additional forms.

subfiles.title: Translation of Mexican note on Enrique Bravo
subfiles.about: English translation requesting permission for Bravo’s commercial assignment in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Mexico seeks a permit enabling Bravo to coordinate renewal of trade with Japan.

subfiles.title: Conversation on missionaries’ food shipments
subfiles.about: Clarifies how much food missionaries may take into Japan.
subfiles.summary: Missionaries may import permitted foods, up to one ton per person annually.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Enrique Bravo application
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Bravo’s completed application and forwards it to military authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Department promises to advise Mexico when the military decision is received.

subfiles.title: Montevideo airgram on Uruguayan commercial delegate
subfiles.about: Reports Carlos Hounie Fleurquin’s appointment and planned voyage to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Uruguay named Consul Hounie commercial delegate to Japan; he and his wife planned to sail for the United States on August 8.

subfiles.title: Panamanian supplementary note enclosing Azrak residence permit
subfiles.about: Supplements Azrak’s application with his 1941 Kobe residence permit.
subfiles.summary: Panama forwards a Japanese residence permit supporting Azrak’s application.

subfiles.title: Translation of supplementary Azrak note
subfiles.about: English translation of the note enclosing Azrak’s residence permit.
subfiles.summary: Vallarino submits Azrak’s 1941 Kobe residence permit as supplementary evidence.

subfiles.title: Restricted background report on Isidoro Azrak
subfiles.about: Provides military authorities with adverse background information relevant to Azrak’s application.
subfiles.summary: The Department reports dubious business reputations and prewar Japanese connections among Azrak family members. It describes Isidoro and Victor Azrak’s trading activities, Isidoro’s Kobe business, wartime visa concerns, and intelligence suspicions, while enclosing the 1941 residence permit.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Azrak residence permit
subfiles.about: Confirms forwarding Azrak’s residence permit to military authorities.
subfiles.summary: The Department reports that Azrak’s residence permit has been added to his case.

subfiles.title: Comments on draft circular airgram for Japan entry permits
subfiles.to: E. Williams III and Richard E. Hibbard
subfiles.about: Suggests revised instructions for foreign-government submission of entry applications to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Wolberg proposes routing non-U.S. applications through governments and questions the twenty-one-day permit validity.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on baggage limits for returning Japanese
subfiles.about: Investigates whether self-financed Japanese returnees face a baggage-weight limit.
subfiles.summary: War Department officials confirm no general baggage limit; 400 pounds applies only aboard Army vessels.

subfiles.title: Uruguayan request to establish a commercial office in Japan
subfiles.about: Requests approval for Carlos Hounie Fleurquin as Uruguay’s Tokyo commercial delegate.
subfiles.summary: Uruguay seeks SCAP approval to establish a Tokyo commercial office and forwards Hounie’s Form DS-513 in duplicate.

subfiles.title: Carlos Hounie Fleurquin application to enter Japan
subfiles.to: Secretary of the Joint Chiefs of Staff
subfiles.about: Requests indefinite entry to Tokyo as Uruguay’s commercial delegate.
subfiles.summary: Hounie applies to reside in Tokyo and establish Uruguay’s proposed commercial office.

subfiles.title: RPA referral of Hounie application
subfiles.about: Forwards Uruguay’s note and Hounie’s application for prompt action.
subfiles.summary: Atwood urges early arrangements because Hounie and his wife planned to sail August 8.

subfiles.title: Translation of Uruguayan commercial-office note
subfiles.about: English translation requesting approval of Uruguay’s Tokyo commercial office and delegate.
subfiles.summary: Mora asks U.S. intercession with SCAP and submits Hounie’s entry application.

subfiles.title: War Department policy message on entry into U.S.-controlled Pacific areas
subfiles.about: Amends policy governing foreign-national entry into U.S.-controlled Pacific territories.
subfiles.summary: Russian and satellite nationals remain excluded from Pacific islands; theater commanders control other foreign entry decisions.

subfiles.title: Conversation about Mrs. Hounie’s accompanying travel
subfiles.about: Discusses submitting Mrs. Hounie’s request despite missing application information.
subfiles.summary: Yriart asks that Hounie’s case and his wife’s accompanying travel be sent immediately to SCAP. Wolberg warns that missing data and military workload may delay a decision but promises efforts to expedite the official case.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Carlos Hounie Fleurquin
subfiles.about: Records security checks concerning Carlos Hounie Fleurquin.
subfiles.summary: Departmental checks found no derogatory information concerning Hounie.

subfiles.title: Memorandum to Uruguay concerning the Hounies
subfiles.about: Confirms immediate referral of Hounie’s application and his wife’s request to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: The Department is sending the commercial-office proposal, Hounie’s application, and Mrs. Hounie’s request without waiting for her missing data. Uruguay is expected to provide that information later.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Hounie application to the War Department
subfiles.about: Requests expedited SCAP action on Hounie and his wife.
subfiles.summary: Hibbard forwards Hounie’s application and notes the couple’s planned August 8 departure.

subfiles.title: Williams memorandum on Japan and Korea entry circulars
subfiles.about: Reports discussions about proposed circular instructions for entry into Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Williams notes unresolved Korean procedures, workload concerns, and the option of issuing separate Japan and Korea airgrams.

subfiles.title: Shanghai inquiry on alien air transit through Japan
subfiles.about: Asks about passport validation and restrictions for aliens transiting Japan by air.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai requests guidance on authorizing and processing non-American air transit through Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply to Shanghai on alien transit query
subfiles.about: Reports that SCAP is being consulted about the transit question.
subfiles.summary: The Department advises Shanghai that it has queried SCAP.

subfiles.title: Manila inquiry on validating alien passports
subfiles.about: Asks whether alien passports may be validated for Japanese air transit like American passports.
subfiles.summary: Manila requests authority to validate aliens’ passports for transit through Japan.

subfiles.title: Airgram to Baghdad concerning Joseph David Isaac
subfiles.about: Requests Iraqi governmental approval and explains quota rules for Isaac’s application.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy must determine whether Iraq approved Isaac’s travel. If approved, the Department will forward his case, while advising that Iraq likely receives only one three-week business permit at a time.

subfiles.title: Reply to Manila on alien transit permits
subfiles.about: Withholds authorization pending instructions and SCAP’s response.
subfiles.summary: Manila is told not to validate alien transit passports until SCAP replies.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Japanese air-transit permits for aliens
subfiles.about: Reviews whether consulates can authorize aliens’ air transit through Japan.
subfiles.summary: State and War officials agree existing authority covers Americans only and seek clarification from Tokyo.

subfiles.title: File memorandum on Joseph David Isaac
subfiles.about: Records checks on Isaac and his Baghdad import-export firm.
subfiles.summary: Departmental searches found no information on Isaac, Moshi, or their firm.

subfiles.title: Baghdad Embassy despatch transmitting Isaac application
subfiles.about: Transmits Isaac’s application in triplicate for a Japanese military entry permit.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy requests SCAP’s decision because Iraq has no representation in Japan.

subfiles.title: Joseph David Isaac application letter
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander of the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests permission to visit Kobe and Osaka to renew prewar textile-import connections.
subfiles.summary: Iraqi merchant Isaac seeks three to six months in Kobe and Osaka to resume textile trade.
